html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. SDK: software development kit; MCP: Model Context Protocol; PR: pull request; JSON: JavaScript Object Notation; API: application programming interface; URL: uniform resource locator

  • For each of the six scenarios: the requirement, the design decisions that the exam tests, and the traps
  • How the ten decision rules show up inside each scenario
  • Which module to reread when a scenario feels weak

On exam day you get four scenarios out of six, in random order; the items inside a scenario can come from different domains. Think "scenario first", then ask which domain the item is really testing.

2Scenario 1: Customer Support Resolution Agent

Requirement: an Agent SDK agent with MCP tools (get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund, escalate_to_human); 80%+ first-contact resolution; knows when to escalate.

Decision Best answer Module
Loop control Continue on tool_use, stop on end_turn 1
Verify the customer before money moves Programmatic prerequisite gate, not a prompt reminder 3
Refund limit Hook that blocks above the limit and redirects to escalation 3
Confusion between similar tools Better tool descriptions first 5
Tool failures Structured errors with category and retryable flag; business errors explain themselves 5
Mixed-up facts in long chats Case-facts block, trimmed tool output 12
When to escalate Explicit criteria + few-shot; honor "get me a person" at once; policy gaps; not sentiment or confidence 13
Handoff Structured summary (customer, root cause, amount, recommended action) 3

Traps: "stronger prompt" for a hard rule; a classifier before criteria; picking one of several customer matches by heuristic.

Exam tip

Support-agent items usually test enforcement (gates and hooks), tool descriptions, escalation criteria and structured errors.

3Scenario 2: Code Generation with Claude Code

Requirement: a team uses Claude Code for generation, refactoring, debugging and docs; custom slash commands, CLAUDE.md, plan mode versus direct execution.

Decision Best answer Module
Team standards Project CLAUDE.md, not user-level 7
Shared command .claude/commands/ in the repository 7
Conventions for files spread everywhere (tests) Path-specific rules with glob patterns 7
Large restructuring Plan mode, then direct execution 8
One-file fix with a stack trace Direct execution 8
Verbose exploration Explore subagent; skill with context: fork 7, 8
Long sessions degrade Scratchpad, subagents, /compact 12
Inconsistent results from prose 2 to 3 input/output examples; tests first; interview 8

Traps: one giant root CLAUDE.md; per-directory CLAUDE.md files for scattered tests; "start direct and switch if it gets hard".

4Scenario 3: Multi-Agent Research System

Requirement: a coordinator delegates to web-search, document-analysis, synthesis and report subagents; cited, comprehensive reports.

Decision Best answer Module
Architecture Hub-and-spoke; all communication through the coordinator 2
Incomplete coverage though subagents succeeded Fix the coordinator's decomposition 2
Passing context Put findings and metadata in the subagent prompt (no inheritance) 2
Parallelism Several Task calls in one response 2
Tool scope Role-specific tools; scoped verify_fact for synthesis 6
Timeouts Structured error context, partial results, coverage annotations 13
Attribution and conflicts Claim-source mappings, both values with dates 14
Context budgets Upstream agents return structured facts, not long text 12

Traps: blaming downstream agents; suppressing a failure as an empty success; aborting the whole run; averaging conflicting statistics.

Exam tip

Research-system items usually test coordinator decomposition, context passing, error context and provenance.

5Scenario 4: Developer Productivity with Claude

Requirement: an SDK agent helps engineers explore unfamiliar code, understand legacy systems, generate boilerplate and automate chores with Read, Write, Bash, Grep and Glob plus MCP servers.

Decision Best answer Module
Find callers of a function Grep the name, then Read to follow flow 6
Find files by pattern Glob 6
Edit fails (non-unique text) Read + Write 6
Shared integrations Project .mcp.json with ${ENV} tokens; community servers for standard tools 6
Agent prefers Grep over a better MCP tool Rich MCP tool description 6
Reduce exploratory calls MCP resources (catalogs) 6
Resuming work Named session; tell it which files changed; fresh summary if stale 4

Traps: reading the whole repository up front; building a custom server for a standard integration.

6Scenario 5: Claude Code for Continuous Integration

Requirement: automated code review, test generation and PR feedback; actionable comments with few false positives.

Decision Best answer Module
Non-interactive run -p 8
Machine-readable findings --output-format json + --json-schema 8
Project context for CI CLAUDE.md (standards, fixtures, criteria) 8
False positives Explicit report/skip criteria; disable a noisy category temporarily; severity examples 9
Format consistency Few-shot with location, issue, severity, fix 9
Duplicate comments after new commits Pass prior findings; report only new 8
Big pull request Per-file passes + integration pass 4, 11
Reviewing generated code Independent instance 8, 11
Cost saving Batch only non-blocking jobs 11

Traps: a confidence cutoff for precision; batch for pre-merge checks; asking the same session to double-check.

7Scenario 6: Structured Data Extraction

Requirement: extract fields from unstructured documents, validate with JSON schemas, keep accuracy high, handle edge cases, feed downstream systems.

Decision Best answer Module
Guaranteed structure Tool use + JSON schema 10
Unknown document type tool_choice: "any" with several schemas 6, 10
Missing data Nullable fields (no fabrication); unclear, other + detail 10
Semantic errors Validation code; calculated_total vs stated_total; conflict_detected 10
Retry With document + failed output + errors; not when the info is absent 10
Bulk processing Batches API with custom_id; resubmit failures; tune on a sample 11
Quality at scale Per-type and per-field accuracy; stratified sampling; calibrated confidence 14
Varied formats Few-shot with different structures 9

Traps: trusting 97% overall accuracy; retrying on absent data; required fields that force invention.

Exam tip

Extraction items usually test tool use with schemas, nullable fields, retry limits, batches and accuracy by segment.

8Exam Q&A

S1(Support agent) Production data shows the agent sometimes issues a refund before checking that the customer owns the order. Which change gives the strongest guarantee?

  • AAdd a bold reminder to the system prompt
  • BProvide five more examples of correct checks in the system prompt of the agent
  • CBlock process_refund in code until the ownership check has succeeded
  • DLower the model temperature
Show the answer

Answer: C. A hard business requirement needs a deterministic gate; the other options reduce but do not remove the failure rate.

S2(Claude Code) Engineers disagree on style because the team's conventions live in one engineer's home-directory configuration. What fixes the root cause?

  • ATurn off Claude Code
  • BAsk each engineer to copy the lead's home-directory file onto their own machine
  • CEmail the conventions to everyone
  • DMove the conventions into the shared project CLAUDE.md or .claude/rules/
Show the answer

Answer: D. User-level configuration is personal; project-level files are shared through version control.

S3(Research system) A subagent succeeds, but the final report lacks citations, because the synthesis subagent received only the instruction to combine findings. What fixes it?

  • APass the findings with source URLs and document names in a structured form inside the synthesis prompt
  • BRun synthesis twice
  • CAdd a longer system prompt to the coordinator
  • DAllow the synthesis agent to read the coordinator's memory and conversation history directly
Show the answer

Answer: A. Subagents do not inherit context; attribution must travel in the prompt.

S4(Developer productivity) The agent must locate every use of applyDiscount and then understand how it is called. What sequence is best?

  • AGrep for applyDiscount, then Read the relevant files to trace the flow
  • BRead all the files in the repository first, and only then search through them
  • CGlob for applyDiscount
  • DRun Bash ls repeatedly
Show the answer

Answer: A. Grep finds content; Read follows the flow; Glob matches names, not contents.

S5(CI) A review bot produces many low-value comments about naming, and developers have stopped reading it. What is the best approach?

  • AInstruct it to be more conservative
  • BAdd a confidence threshold of 9 out of 10 and drop every finding that scores below it
  • CAdd explicit criteria for what to report and skip, and temporarily disable the naming category while improving it
  • DRun the review twice
Show the answer

Answer: C. Categorical criteria and temporarily disabling a noisy category restore trust.

S6(Extraction) A pipeline reports 98% accuracy overall, but receipts from one retailer are mostly wrong. What should the team do before reducing human review?

  • ARemove review entirely, because an overall accuracy of 98 percent is clearly high enough
  • BMeasure accuracy by document type and field, and keep sampling
  • CRetrain the model
  • DIncrease batch size
Show the answer

Answer: B. Aggregate accuracy hides weak segments; validate per segment and keep sampling.

9Quick Reference Card

Scenario Remember
1 Support agent Gate + hook for hard rules; descriptions; structured errors; case facts; criteria + few-shot escalation; structured handoff
2 Claude Code Project CLAUDE.md; commands in repo; path rules; plan vs direct; fork/Explore
3 Multi-agent research Hub-and-spoke; decomposition; context in prompts; scoped tools; error context; provenance
4 Developer productivity Grep → Read; Glob; Read + Write; .mcp.json; MCP resources; sessions
5 CI -p; JSON schema output; CLAUDE.md; explicit criteria; few-shot; per-file + integration; independent review; batch non-blocking only
6 Extraction Tool use + schema; nullable; validation + retry; batches; segment accuracy; calibrated confidence
